slides.title: Reading Input
slides.content: Console.ReadLine reads text input from the user. It pauses execution until the user presses Enter, then returns the entered text as a string.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

exercise.prompt: What method reads a line of text from the console?

slides.title: Prompting Users
slides.content: Always prompt the user before calling ReadLine so they know what to enter. Use Console.Write to keep the cursor on the same line as the prompt.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

exercise.prompt: Which method keeps the cursor on the same line as your prompt?

slides.title: Parsing Input
slides.content: Since ReadLine returns a string, use int.Parse, double.Parse, or Convert methods to convert the input to numeric types.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

slides.title: Safe Parsing with TryParse
slides.content: TryParse attempts to convert a string and returns a boolean. It is safer than Parse because it does not throw exceptions on invalid input.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

exercise.prompt: What does int.TryParse return on success?

slides.title: Combining Input and Output
slides.content: Real programs combine prompts, input, parsing, and output. Chain these steps to build interactive console applications.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

slides.title: Reading Multiple Inputs
slides.content: You can read multiple values by calling ReadLine multiple times or by reading one line and splitting it into parts.
slides.exampleOutput: Interactive: reads user input, so output depends on input.

exercise.prompt: Complete the split and parse sequence.

slides.title: Converting Input Types
slides.content: Use Parse, TryParse, or Convert classes to turn string input into the desired type. Choose based on whether you need exception handling or safe failure.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Which method does NOT throw on invalid input?

slides.title: Practice: User Input
slides.content: Build a small program that asks for a user's birth year, calculates their age, and prints it. Use int.Parse and arithmetic.

exercise.prompt: Prompt for a number, parse it, add 10, and print the result.
hints: Read with Console.ReadLine, convert the value, add 10, and print it.
Check that your code uses the required keywords listed in the exercise.

slides.title: Flow Builder: Input and Output
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to read a value and print it back out.
